Inaian Standard 

METHODS OF TEST FOR 
PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS 

[ P : 92 ] 

CONE PENETRATION OF PETROLATUM 

UDG 665-772-3 : 539*57 ' 

Adapted from Joint Publication ASTM Designation D 937-771 
IP Designation 179 168 

1. SCOPE 

1,1 This method of test is intended for use in measuring with a penetro- 
meter the penetration of petrolatum as an empirical measure of consistency 
( j^^Note). 

Note — This procedure is applicable to petrolatums having penetrations up to 
350. A sample of 2 kg is required. For petrolatums having penetrations less than 
200 one-third of this quantity is adequate. 

2. DEFINITION 

2.1 Penetration of Petrolatum — It is defined as the depth, in tenths 
of a millimetre, that a standard cone will penetrate the sample under fixed 
conditions of mass, time and temperature. 

3. OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 

3.1 The sample is melted, heated to 82°C and then cooled under con- 
trolled conditions to 25°G. The penetration is measured with the cone 
and the sample at this temperature using a penetrometer by means of 
which a standard cone is applied to the sample for 5 seconds under a load 
of 150 g,

4. APPARATUS 

4.1 Penetrometer and Cone — same as described in IS ; 1448 
[P:60]-1971*. 

4.2 Oven — capable of maintaining a temperature of 82 ± 2°G for 
melting the petrolatum samples. 

4.3 Water Bath — a constant temperature water bath regulated to 
25 ± 0*5°G. 

4.4 Sample Containers — cylindrical, having a fiat bottom, 100 ± 6 
mm diameter and 65 mm or more in depth, constructed of at least 
1*6 mm metal and provided with a well fitting water-tight cover 
( see Note ) . 

Note — Containers of the * ointment box ' type having somewhat flexible sides 
should not be used, for these permit slight working of the petrolatum, due to flexing 
of the sides in handling. 

5. PREPARATION OF SAMPLE 

5.1 Test all samples of petrolatum for original consistency after melting 
and cooling to the temperature of the test as described in 5.3. 

5.2 If the penetration of the sample is over 200, three separate test 
samples are required, 

5.3 Melt the sample in an oven maintained at 82 ± 2°G {see Note 1 ). 
Place the required number of sample containers in the oven along with 
the sample to bring them up to 82°G. When the sample has melted and 
comes to within S^'G of the temperature, remove the sample and the 
heated containers and fill the required number of containers to within 
6 mm of their rims. Allow the filled containers to cool in a location free 
from draughts and at a temperature controlled to 25 ± 2°C for 16 to 18 
hours. Then place the samples in the water bath for 2 hours to bring the 
temperature to 25 ± 0'5°G before testing ( see Note 2 ). 

Note 1 — Some petrolatums containing higher melting point waxes may 
require higher pouring temperatures. 

Note 2 — Some compounded petrolatums are affected on contact with w^ater. 
Such samples shall be covered with a sealed lid as required for greases. Uncom- 
pounded petrolatums are not affected by water and need not be covered. 

6. PROCEDURE 

6.1 The surface of the sample shall not be cut level nor worked in any 
other way, as this may affect the result. If the temperature of the 

♦Methods of test for petroleum and its products: [ P : 60] Consistency of lubricating 
grease by cone penetrometer (first revision ). 



IS :144a tP:d2].1d79 

penetrometer cone ( that is, the room temperature ) varies from 25°G by 
2'^G or more, adjust the cone temperature to 25 i 0'5°G immediately 
before testing the sample. Frequent adjustment of the cone temperature 
may be necessary if the room temperature varies appreciably from 25^C. 

6.2 Place the container filled with the sample on the penetrometer table, 
so located that the tip of the penetrometer cone is 25 to 40 mm in from 
the rim of the container ( except for petrolatums having a penetration 
greater than 200) {see6A), Observe that the cone is in its 'zero' 
position and adjust either the indicator assembly or the table, dependent 
on the type of instrument, until the tip of the cone just touches the surface 
of the sample. Watching the shadow of the tip is an aid to accurate 
setting. Finally, quickly release the plunger and hold for 5 seconds. Read 
the total penetration from the scale. Make at least three determinations. 

6*3 With samples having penetrations less than 200, three tests ( and 
sometimes more ) may be made in one container by proper spacing. To 
prevent one test from being affected by the disturbed area of a previous 
test the tip of the cone shall not be placed nearer the edge of a previous 
test than the penetration distance of the sample. Some harder petrolatums 
tend to form a marked depression in the centre on solidifying; such 
samples should not be tested in this depression, as the results obtained 
may be different from those obtained in off-centre positions on the level 
surface. 

6-4 With samples having penetrations over 200, make only one test in a 
container and place the cone tip as exactly as possible at the centre of the 
container. 

7. REPORT 

7.1 Report the average of all results to the nearest 0*1 mm, as the 
penetration. 

8. PRECISION 

8.1 Results of duplicate test ( each based on the average of three indivi- 
dual values ) shall not differ by more than the following amounts: 

Repeatability Reproducibility 

2 + ( 5 percent ) 9 + ( 12 percent)
